body:
Kendrick and Eldering spent many long nights
studying the bacteria and finally
produced a
potential vaccine. Before they performed any clinical
trials, though, they had to be certain ⓐ[that /
which] it would not have any negative side effects
on the subjects. They ran many laboratory tests,
and they even injected it into ⓑ[them / themselves]
to confirm that it was safe. From 1934 to 1935,
they conducted their first field test with 1,592
children. In the group of 712 ⓒ[vaccinating /
vaccinated] children, only four developed whooping
cough, and none of these cases were serious.
Despite the apparent (A)[failure / success] of the
vaccine, Kendrick and Eldering wanted further confirmation of its effectiveness. They became
determined to (B)[expand / suspend] their research and
run more tests with larger groups of children. However,
they were (C)[able / unable] to proceed because they
were facing a severe lack of funds. With thousands of
children continuing to suffer from the disease, they
found themselves in a desperate situation.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: successexpandunable
failureexpandunable
successexpandable
failuresuspendunable
successsuspendable
solution: (A) 첫 현장 실험에서 백신을 접종한 712명의 아이들의 그룹 중 단지 4명만 백일해에 걸렸고, 그 가운데 심각한 사례는 없 었다고 했으므로, 백신이 분명히 성공했다는 흐름이 되어야 한 다. 따라서 success(성공)가 알맞다. (B) 앞서 Kendrick과 Eldering이 백신의 효과에 대한 추가 확인 을 원했다고 했으며, 뒤에는 그들이 더 큰 그룹의 어린이들을 대상으로 더 많은 실험을 진행하기로 했다는 내용이 언급되므 로, 연구의 크기를 확대하기로 결심했다는 흐름이 되어야 한 다. 따라서 expand(~을 확대[확장]하다)가 알맞다. (C) 그들은 심각한 자금 부족에 직면하고 있었다고 했으므로, 연구와 실험을 계속 진행할 수 없었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 unable(~할 수 없는)이 알맞다.

body:
By 1937, Kendrick and Eldering were able to
include more than 4,200 children in their trial. Just
as in their first field test, the vaccinated group
demonstrated a (A)[high / low] level of immunity
against the disease. The scientific community was
ⓐamazed at the results, and, in 1940, the vaccine
started being distributed all across the United
States. Four years later, it ⓑwas added to the
American Medical Association’s list of recommended
immunizations, and soon after, there was a dramatic
(B)[decline / increase] in whooping cough infections.
In the mid-1970s, the number of annual deaths
caused by whooping cough, which ⓒhad reached
7,518 in 1934, dropped to under 10.
Kendrick and Eldering ㉠그들이 백신으로 특허를 받
았더라면 매우 부유해질 수도 있었을 것이라는 말을
자주 들었다. However, they replied that it had not
been created by them alone, but with the help of
many others. They also avoided personal interviews,
not ⓓwanted to reveal the great contribution they
had made. They said that they had genuinely
enjoyed the challenge of creating the vaccine, so
the excessive praise that they received made them
(C)[comfortable / uncomfortable]. In the end,
knowing that so many lives ⓔwere being saved
thanks to their hard work was enough of a reward
for these remarkable and modest heroes.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: highincreaseuncomfortable
lowdeclinecomfortable
highdeclinecomfortable
lowincreaseuncomfortable
highdeclineuncomfortable
solution: (A) 과학계는 그 결과에 깜짝 놀랐고, 1940년에 백신이 미국 전 역으로 배포되기 시작했다고 했으므로, 현장 실험에서 백신을 접 종한 그룹은 질병에 대해 높은 수준의 면역력을 보여주었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 high(높은)가 알맞다. (B) 1934년에 7,518명에 달했던 백일해로 인한 연간 사망자 수가 1970년대 중반에 10명 미만으로 떨어졌다고 했으므로, 백신이 미국 의학 협회의 권장 예방접종 목록에 추가된 지 얼마 지나지 않아 백일해 감염은 극적으로 감소했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 decline(감소)이 알맞다. (C) Kendrick과 Eldering은 자신들의 큰 공헌을 드러내고 싶지 않 아 개인적인 인터뷰를 피했다는 내용에 이어, 그들이 진정으로 백신을 만드는 도전을 즐겼다고 말했다고 한 뒤에 so(그래서)로 이어지므로, 지나친 칭찬은 그들을 불편하게 만든다고 말했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 uncomfortable(불편한)이 알맞다.

body:
By 1937, Kendrick and Eldering were able to include
more than 4,200 children in their trial. Just as in their
first field test, the vaccinated group demonstrated a
high level of immunity against the disease. The
scientific community was amazed at the results, and,
in 1940, the vaccine started ⓐto be distributed all
across the United States. Four years later, it was
added to the American Medical Association’s list of
ⓑrecommended immunizations, and soon after, there
was a dramatic decline in whooping cough infections.
In the mid-1970s, the number of annual deaths
caused by whooping cough, which had reached 7,518
in 1934, ⓒdropping to under 10.
Kendrick and Eldering were often told that they
could have become very wealthy if they had
patented their vaccine. However, they replied that it
had not ⓓbeen created by them alone, but (A)[with
/ without] the help of many others. They also
(B)[avoided / welcomed] personal interviews, not
wanting to reveal the great contribution they ⓔhad
been made. They said that they had genuinely
enjoyed the challenge of creating the vaccine, so
the excessive praise ⓕthat they received made
them uncomfortable. In the end, knowing that so
many lives were being saved thanks to their hard
work ⓖwas enough of a reward for these
remarkable and (C)[modest / arrogant] heroes.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)               (B)
(C)
choices: withwelcomedarrogant

solution: (A) 앞서 Kendrick과 Eldering은 백신을 둘이서만 만든 것이 아 니라고 했으므로, ‘not A, but B(A가 아니라, B)의 구조에 의해 둘만이 아니라 다른 많은 사람들의 도움으로 만들어졌다고 답 했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 with(~으로)가 알맞다. (B) Kendrick과 Eldering은 자신들의 큰 공헌을 드러내길 원치 않았다고 했으므로, 개인적인 인터뷰를 피했다는 흐름이 되어 야 한다. 따라서 avoided(~을 피했다)가 알맞다. (C) Kendrick과 Eldering은 지나친 칭찬은 그들을 불편하게 만 든다고 말했다고 했으므로, 그들을 겸손한 영웅들로 언급하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 modest(겸손한)가 알맞다.

body:
Pearl Kendrick studied bacteriology in university and
ⓐwas recruited by the Michigan Department of
Health in 1920. It was there ⓑthat she met fellow
bacteriologist Grace Eldering. The two quickly bonded,
and in 1932 they started working (A)[together /
separately] on a vaccine for whooping cough.
Personal experience served as motivation for both of
them, as they had each survived whooping cough as
children ⓒitself and (B)[forgot / remembered] the
severe pain of the disease. Both scientists were also
eager to promote children’s health.
Unfortunately, research funding was extremely
limited due to the Great Depression. Also, Kendrick
and Eldering had to develop the vaccine as a
(C)[main / side] project. It was like having a second
job for ⓓwhich they never received any payment.
Still, when they finished their normal duties each
day, they would get started on the work that they
were enthusiastic about. The difficulties they faced
did not stop them from persisting toward their
goal. They did not do the work to make extra
money; instead, they worked ⓔto relieve the
suffering of innocent children and their families.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: togetherforgotmain
separatelyrememberedside

togetherrememberedside
solution: (A) Pearl Kendrick과 Grace Eldering을 가리키는 they(그들)가 빠 르게 유대감을 형성했다고 한 뒤에 and(그리고)로 연결되며, 개 인적 경험이 두 사람 모두에게 (연구에 대한) 동기가 되었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 1932년에 백일해 백신을 함께 연구하기 시 작했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 together(함께)가 알맞다. (B) 앞서 백일해에 대한 개인적 경험이 두 사람 모두에게 연구 에 대한 동기가 되었다고 했으며, 뒤에서는 두 과학자가 아이들 의 건강을 증진시키기를 간절히 바랐다고 했으므로, 자신들이 몸소 겪은 그 질병(백일해)의 극심한 고통을 기억하고 있었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 remembered(기억했다)가 알맞다. (C) 그것은 마치 어떠한 보수도 받지 못하는 두 번째 직업을 갖는 것과 같았다고 뒤에서 말하므로, Kendrick과 Eldering이 본업 외에 부가적인 프로젝트로서 백신을 개발해야 했다는 흐 름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 side(종속적인; 부업의)가 알맞다.

Kendrick and Eldering spent many long nights
studying the bacteria and finally
produced a
potential vaccine. Before they performed any clinical
trials, though, they had to be certain ⓐ[that /
which] it would not have any negative side effects
on the subjects. They ran many laboratory tests,
and they even injected it into ⓑ[them / themselves]
to confirm that it was safe. From 1934 to 1935,
they conducted their first field test with 1,592
children. In the group of 712 ⓒ[vaccinating /
vaccinated] children, only four developed whooping
cough, and none of these cases were serious.
Despite the apparent (A)[failure / success] of the
vaccine, Kendrick and Eldering wanted further confirmation of its effectiveness. They became
determined to (B)[expand / suspend] their research and
run more tests with larger groups of children. However,
they were (C)[able / unable] to proceed because they
were facing a severe lack of funds. With thousands of
children continuing to suffer from the disease, they
found themselves in a desperate situation.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
choices: thatthemvaccinating
whichthemselvesvaccinated
thatthemselvesvaccinating
whichthemvaccinated
thatthemselvesvaccinated

By 1937, Kendrick and Eldering were able to
include more than 4,200 children in their trial. Just
as in their first field test, the vaccinated group
demonstrated a high level of immunity against the
disease. The scientific community was amazed at
the results, and, in 1940, the vaccine started being
distributed all across the United States. Four years
later, it was added to the American Medical
Association’s list of recommended immunizations,
and soon after, there was a dramatic decline in
whooping cough infections. In the mid-1970s, the
number of annual deaths caused by whooping
cough, which had reached 7,518 in 1934, dropped
to under 10.

Pertussis is a bacterial disease characterized by serious coughing, breathing difficulties, and the high-pitched “whooping” sound that people with the disease make as they try to breathe in. Because of this distinct sound, people started to call the disease “whooping cough.” For a long time, this terrible illness was one of the greatest terrors of (A)__________________________________, because babies who contracted it had a high chance of dying. In the 1930s, an average of 6,000 people died of whooping cough in the United States each year. Ninety-five percent of them were children under five years of age. The cause of the disease had been identified in 1906, but the vaccines that had been developed were ineffective. Scientists and researchers worked for more than 20 years to produce an effective one, but their efforts were fruitless — until Kendrick and Eldering came along.

When we think about science, we might consider
it as a domain reserved exclusively for scientists in
long, white lab coats who spend their days
conducting experiments and analyzing data. They
seem to have very little in common with ordinary
people like us. However, this perception is (A)[close
to / far from] the truth. In reality, science belongs
to everyone, and we all have the ability to play a
role in the advancement of science. There have
been numerous citizen science projects in which
ordinary people have made contributions to
remarkable scientific accomplishments. Let’s take a
look at two of them.
Kevin Schawinski was a young (B)[astrology /
astronomy] researcher studying black holes and the
evolution of galaxies at the University of Oxford.
This might sound exciting, but his job there was
dull and time-consuming. He had to classify around
one million images of galaxies according to their
shape. Since they all looked similar but were

click buttons that described its features. Is the

body:
Chasing Steve
In Alberta, Canada, there were some “aurora chasers” who formed an informal group online. They would leave their homes at night and try to get exceptional photographs of auroras. Then they would share them with the rest of the group. In the summer of 2014, the group members began to notice something strange appearing in the night sky. There were unusual ribbons of green and purple light, some of which seemed to stretch for thousands of kilometers. Sometimes they lasted for just a few minutes, while other times they remained in the sky for a whole hour. They were similar in appearance to auroras, yet they possessed some notably different features. (A)______________________________, the group decided to name the phenomenon “Steve,” based on a scene from an animated movie in which some characters give that name to an unfamiliar object.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

Never questioning their identity
Not recognizing their importance
Inspired by their scientific findings
Convinced the mystery had been solved
solution:

2. 그래서 낯선 물체에 ‘Steve’라는 이름을 붙이는 애니메이션 장면을 따라 그 현상을 ‘Steve’라 불렀다 — 정체를 몰랐다는 뜻이다.
3. 따라서 빈칸에는 ‘그것들이 무엇인지 확신하지 못해서(Unsure of what they were)’가 알맞다. 정체를 의심하지 않음(②)·수수께끼가 풀렸다고 확신함(⑤)은 반대이다.
4. 따라서 답은 ①이다.

choices: Trevor had a rough appearance with a bushy red beard.
Trevor's paintings were in great demand among buyers.
Trevor received a penny an hour for painting the beggar.

Hughie shook hands with Trevor when he arrived at the studio.
solution:

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
어법상 알맞은 것은 ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓓ이다.
ⓐ find의 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어 Trevor가 '앉아 있는' 주체이므로 현재분사는 알맞게 쓰였다.
ⓒ 의문형용사 what이 명사 prospects를 수식하여 의문사구 what prospects를 이루고, ‘의문사구+주어+동사’의 어순인 what prospects you have로 쓰였으므로 알맞다.
ⓓ find의 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어 him이 '기다리고 있는' 주체이므로 현재분사는 알맞게 쓰였다.
오답
ⓑ to finish → finished (get의 목적어 the picture가 '완성되는' 대상이므로 목적격보어 자리에 과거분사를 쓴다.)

ⓕ man → men ('가장 ~한 것 중 하나'를 뜻하는 ‘one of the+최상급+복수명사’ 구조이므로 복수형으로 고친다.)

“What on earth do you mean?” shouted Hughie.
“The old man you saw today in the studio,” said Trevor, “was Baron* Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, and he buys all my pictures. He gave me a commission to paint him as a beggar. And I must say he looked magnificent in his rags. (A)______; they are an old suit I got in Spain.”
“Baron Hausberg!” cried Hughie. “Good heavens! I gave him a gold coin!” Hughie sank into the chair in shock.
“A gold coin!” shouted Trevor and burst out laughing.
“You should have told me, Alan,” said Hughie. “Now I’ve made a fool of myself.”
“Well, when you came in, I didn’t know whether Hausberg would like his name mentioned. After all, he wasn’t fully dressed.”
“What a fool he must think I am!” said Hughie.
“Not at all. He was in the highest spirits after you left. He kept smiling to himself and rubbing his old, wrinkled hands together. I couldn’t understand why he was so interested to know all about you, but I see it all now.”
Hughie sighed. “The best thing I can do is go to bed,” he said. “And my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone.” Hughie walked home feeling very unhappy.
*baron 남작

choices: Or perhaps I should say in my rags

He had borrowed them from another model

solution:
빈칸 뒤에서 그 옷이 자신이 스페인에서 구한 낡은 정장이라고 밝히고 있으므로, 앞서 '그의 누더기'라고 말한 것을 '내 누더기'로 바로잡는 내용이 와야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ① '아니, 어쩌면 내 누더기라고 말해야겠군'이 알맞다.

② 그는 그 옷을 여러 해 동안 입었음이 틀림없다

④ 그는 그것을 다른 모델에게서 빌렸다
⑤ 하지만 나는 그런 옷을 절대 직접 입지 않을 것이다

(4) Hughie wanted Alan to share the story of the gold coin with others.

solution:
(1) Trevor는 Hughie가 남작에게 준 금화에 대해 들었을 때 갑자기 웃기 시작했다.

body:
Hughie Erskine was a ⓐwonderfully good-looking man, with crisp brown hair, a sculpture-like profile, and grey eyes. He had every accomplishment except ⓑthat of making money. He lived on two hundred pounds a year ⓒwhen an old aunt gave him. He had tried everything. He had gone to the stock exchange for six months. He ⓓhad been a tea merchant for a little longer. Ultimately, he became nothing. He was a delightful, incompetent young man with a perfect profile and no profession.
ⓔTo make matters worse, he was in love. The girl he loved was Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loved Hughie, too, and the colonel was very fond of him. However, he would not hear of any engagement. He would say “Come to me, my boy, when you have got ten thousand pounds of your own, and we will talk about it.”
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ when → which 또는 that (선행사 two hundred pounds a year를 수식하는 관계사절에서 타동사 gave의 직접목적어가 빠져 있으므로, 관계부사 when을 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that으로 고친다. 관계사절의 him은 간접목적어이다.)
오답
ⓐ 형용사 good-looking을 꾸미는 부사 wonderfully는 적절하다.
ⓑ that은 앞의 단수명사 accomplishment를 대신하며, of making money가 뒤에서 수식한다.
ⓓ 과거의 경험을 서술하는 흐름에서 그보다 앞선 일을 나타내고 있으므로 과거완료 had been은 적절하다.
ⓔ '설상가상으로'라는 뜻의 독립부정사를 이루므로, To make는 알맞게 쓰였다.

body:
One morning, Hughie dropped in ⓐto see a great friend of him, Alan Trevor. Trevor was a painter. He was a strange, rough fellow with a bushy red beard. However, when he took up the brush, he was a real master, and his pictures were eagerly sought after.
When Hughie came into the studio, he found Trevor ⓑputting the finishing touches on a wonderful life-size picture of a beggar. The beggar was standing on a raised platform in a corner of the studio. He was a wrinkly old man with a pitiful expression. He wore a ragged brown cape, and he leaned on a rough stick with one hand while ⓒheld out his hat for donations with the other.
“What an amazing model!” said Hughie, as he shook hands with his friend. “ⓓWhat miserable he looks! How much does the model get for posing?”
“A penny an hour.”
“And how much do you get for your painting, Alan?”
“Oh, I get two thousand pounds for this!”
“Well, I think the model should have a share,” cried Hughie, ⓔlaughed. “He is working ⓕjust as hardly as you!”
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 5개이다.
ⓐ of him → of his (a friend와 소유격의 의미를 함께 나타내는 이중소유격이므로 of 뒤에 소유대명사를 쓴다.)
ⓒ held → holding (while이 이끄는 분사구문에서 주어 he가 모자를 '내밀고 있는' 주체이므로 현재분사로 고친다.)
ⓓ What → How (뒤에 형용사 miserable이 이어지므로 「How+형용사+주어+동사」 어순의 감탄문을 이끄는 How로 고친다.)
ⓔ laughed → laughing (주어 Hughie가 '웃는' 주체이므로 분사구문을 이끄는 현재분사로 고친다.)
ⓕ hardly → hard ('열심히'라는 뜻의 부사는 hard이며, hardly는 '거의 ~않다'라는 뜻이므로 원급 비교 구문의 문맥에 맞지 않는다.)
오답
ⓑ find의 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어 Trevor가 마무리 작업을 '하고 있는' 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 지닌 현재분사 putting은 알맞게 쓰였다.

“Don’t run away, Hughie,” he said as he went out. “I will be back in a moment.”

(A)그가 찾을 수 있었던 것은 몇 개의 동전뿐이었다. “Poor old fellow,” he thought to himself. “He needs money ⓒmore than I do.” He walked across the studio and slipped a gold coin into the beggar’s hand.

body:
That night, about eleven o’clock, he wandered into a café and found Trevor ⓐ[sat / sitting] by himself.
“Well, Alan, did you get the picture ⓑ[finishing / finished] all right?” he asked.
“Finished and framed, my boy!” answered Trevor. “And, by the way, the old model you saw ⓒ[is / are] quite curious about you. I had to tell him all about you: who you are, where you live, what your income is, and what prospects you have.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I will probably find him waiting for me when I get home. Poor old man! (A)내가 그를 위해 무언가를 해 줄 수 있다면 좋을 텐데. I think it is (B)[dreadful / fortunate] that anyone should be so miserable. I have piles of old clothes at home. Do you think he would care for any of them? His rags were falling to bits.”
“But he looks (C)[marvelous / unattractive] in them,” said Trevor. “I wouldn’t paint him in a fancy coat for anything. I’ll tell him about your offer, though. By the way, tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”
“What? Did you even tell him about her?” asked Hughie.
“Of course! He knows all about the strict colonel, the charming Laura, and the ten thousand pounds.”
“You told that old beggar about my private affairs?” cried Hughie, looking very red and (D)[irritated / delighted].
“My dear boy,” said Trevor, smiling. “That old beggar, as you call him, is (E)______. He could buy all of London tomorrow with the money in his account.”
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: sat finished is
sitting finishing are
sat finishing are
sitting finished are
sitting finished is
solution:
ⓐ ‘find+목적어+목적격보어’(~가 …하고 있는 것을 발견하다) 구조에서 목적어 Trevor가 혼자 ‘앉아 있는’ 주체이므로, 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 sitting이 알맞다.
ⓑ ‘get+목적어+목적격보어’(~을 …되게 하다) 구조에서 목적어 the picture가 ‘완성되는’ 대상이므로 과거분사 finished가 알맞다.
ⓒ 주어는 명사구 the old model이며, 중심 명사 model이 단수이므로 단수동사 is가 알맞다. you saw는 목적격 관계대명사가 생략된 관계사절로, the old model을 수식한다.

That night, about eleven o’clock, he wandered into a café and found Trevor sitting ⓐby himself.
“Well, Alan, did you get the picture finished all right?” he asked.
“ⓑFinished and framed, my boy!” answered Trevor. “And, by the way, the old model you saw is quite curious about you. I had to tell him all about you: who you are, where you live, what your income is, and what prospects you have.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I will probably find him waiting for me when I get home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I think ⓒthat is dreadful that anyone should be so miserable. I have piles of old clothes at home. Do you think he would care for any of them? His rags were falling to bits.”
“But he looks marvelous in them,” said Trevor. “I wouldn’t paint him in a fancy coat for anything. I’ll tell him about your offer, though. By the way, tell me ⓓhow is Laura. The old model was quite interested in her.”
“What? Did you even tell him about her?” asked Hughie.
“Of course! He knows all about the strict colonel, the charming Laura, and the ten thousand pounds.”
“You told that old beggar about my private affairs?” cried Hughie, ⓔlooked very red and irritated.
“My dear boy,” said Trevor, smiling. “That old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He could buy all of London tomorrow with the money in his account.”
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ that → it (뒤에 이어지는 that절이 진주어이므로 가주어 자리에는 it을 쓴다.)
ⓓ how is Laura → how Laura is (tell의 직접목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문이므로 ‘의문사+주어+동사’ 어순으로 고친다.)
ⓔ looked → looking (주어 Hughie가 얼굴이 붉어지고 짜증이 난 상태로 '보이는' 주체이므로 분사구문을 이끄는 현재분사로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 전치사 by와 재귀대명사가 결합한 by oneself가 '혼자서'라는 뜻으로 쓰였으므로 알맞게 쓰였다.
ⓑ ‘주어+be동사’가 생략된 형태로, 그림이 '완성되고 액자에 끼워진' 대상이므로 과거분사는 알맞게 쓰였다.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A)　　　　 (B)　　　(C)
choices: eager　risen　miserable
eager　raised　miserably
eagerly　raised　miserably
eagerly　risen　miserable
eagerly　raised　miserable
solution:

(C) look이 ‘~하게 보이다’라는 뜻으로 쓰여 주어 he의 상태를 설명하는 보어가 필요하므로 형용사 miserable이 알맞다. ‘How+형용사+주어+동사!’ 구조의 감탄문이다.

“What on earth do you mean?” shouted Hughie.
“The old man ㉠whom you saw today in the studio,” said Trevor, “was Baron* Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, and he buys all my pictures. He gave me a ⓐcommission to paint him as a beggar. And I must say he looked ⓑmagnificent in his rags. Or perhaps I should say in my ⓒrags; they are an old suit I got in Spain.”
“Baron Hausberg!” cried Hughie. “Good heavens! I gave him a gold coin!” Hughie sank into the chair in shock.
“A gold coin!” shouted Trevor and ㉡bursting out laughing.
“(A)너는 나에게 말해 주었어야 한다, Alan,” said Hughie. “Now I’ve made a fool of myself.”
“Well, when you came in, I didn’t know whether Hausberg would like his name ㉢mentioning. After all, he wasn’t fully dressed.”
“What a fool he must think I am!” said Hughie.
“Not at all. He was in the highest ⓓspirits after you left. He kept smiling to ㉣himself and rubbing his old, ⓔwrinkled hands together. I couldn’t understand why he was so ㉤interesting to know all about you, but I see it all now.”
Hughie sighed. “(B)내가 할 수 있는 가장 최선의 일은 잠자리에 드는 것이다,” he said. “And my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone.” Hughie walked home ㉥feeling very unhappy.
*baron 남작
윗글의 밑줄 친 ㉠~㉥ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
어법상 알맞은 것은 ㉠, ㉣, ㉥이다.
㉠ 선행사 The old man 뒤에서 saw의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절이 이어지므로, 목적격 관계대명사 whom은 알맞게 쓰였다.
본문변형 ㉠은 목적격 관계대명사로 원래 지문에서 생략되어 있음
㉣ smiling의 의미상 주어인 He와 같은 대상을 가리키므로, 재귀대명사 himself는 알맞게 쓰였다.
㉥ 완전한 절에 이어지는 분사구문을 이끄는 준동사 자리이다. 주어 Hughie가 '느끼는' 주체이므로, 분사구문을 이끄는 현재분사 feeling은 알맞게 쓰였다.
오답
㉡ bursting → burst (등위접속사 and로 앞의 과거형 동사 shouted와 병렬을 이루므로 과거형으로 고친다.)
㉢ mentioning → mentioned (‘would like+목적어+목적격보어’(~가 …하는 것을 원하다) 구조에서 목적어 his name이 ‘언급되는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분사 mentioned로 고친다.)
㉤ interesting → interested (주어 he가 '관심을 갖게 된' 대상이므로 과거분사형 형용사로 고친다.)

“You should have told me, Alan,” said Hughie. “Now I’ve made ⓐa success of myself.”
“Well, when you came in, (A)나는 Hausberg가 자신의 이름이 언급되는 것을 좋아할지 아닐지 몰랐네. After all, he wasn’t fully dressed.”

Hughie sighed. “The best thing I can do is go to bed,” he said. “And my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone.” Hughie walked home feeling very ⓓhappy.
The next morning, as Hughie was at breakfast, a servant brought him a card on which was written “Monsieur* Gustave Naudin, messenger from Baron Hausberg.”
“I suppose he has come for an apology,” said Hughie to himself, and he told the servant to let the visitor in.
An old gentleman with gold spectacles and grey hair came into the room and said, “Do I have the honor of addressing Monsieur Erskine?”
Hughie bowed.
“I have come from Baron Hausberg,” continued the messenger. “The Baron — ”

“The Baron,” said the old gentleman, with a smile, “has ⓕcommissioned me to bring you this letter,” and he handed a sealed envelope to Hughie.

He had every accomplishment except (B)[that / those] of making money. He lived on two hundred pounds a year (C)[what / that] an old aunt gave him. He had tried everything. He had gone to the stock exchange for six months. He had been a tea merchant for a little longer. Ultimately, he became nothing. He was a delightful, incompetent young man with a perfect profile and no profession.
To make matters worse, he was in love. The girl he loved was Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loved Hughie, too, and the colonel was very fond of him. However, he would not hear of any engagement. He would say “Come to me, my boy, ⓐ______, and we will talk about it.”

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) / (B) / (C)
choices: wonderful / that / what
wonderful / those / that
wonderfully / those / what
wonderfully / that / what
wonderfully / that / that
solution:
(A) 뒤의 형용사 good-looking을 수식하는 자리이므로 부사 wonderfully가 적절하다.
(B) 앞에 나온 단수명사 accomplishment를 대신하는 대명사 자리이므로 단수형 that이 적절하다.
(C) 선행사 two hundred pounds a year가 있고, 뒤에 gave의 직접목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절이 이어지므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 앞에 별도의 선행사를 두지 않는다.

After some time, a servant came in and told Trevor that the frame maker wanted to speak to him.
“Don’t run away, Hughie,” he said as he went out. “I will be back in a moment.”
The old beggar took advantage of Trevor’s absence to rest for a moment on a bench that was behind him. He looked so exhausted and miserable that Hughie ______. Hughie reached into his pocket to see how much money he had. All he could find was a few coins. “Poor old fellow,” he thought to himself. “He needs money more than I do.” He walked across the studio and slipped a gold coin into the beggar’s hand.
The old man was startled, and a faint smile came across his dry lips. “Thank you, sir,” he said. “Thank you.”
When Trevor returned, Hughie said goodbye and left the studio, blushing a little at what he had done, and he walked home.

That night, about eleven o’clock, he wandered into a café and found Trevor sitting by himself.
“Well, Alan, did you get the picture finished all right?” he asked.
“Finished and framed, my boy!” answered Trevor.
(A)
“You told that old beggar about my private affairs?” cried Hughie, looking very red and irritated.
“My dear boy,” said Trevor, smiling. “That old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He could buy all of London tomorrow with the money in his account.”
(B)
“But he looks marvelous in them,” said Trevor. “I wouldn’t paint him in a fancy coat for anything. I’ll tell him about your offer, though. By the way, tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”
“What? Did you even tell him about her?” asked Hughie.
“Of course! He knows all about the strict colonel, the charming Laura, and the ten thousand pounds.”
(C)
“And, by the way, the old model you saw is quite curious about you. I had to tell him all about you: who you are, where you live, what your income is, and what prospects you have.”
(D)
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “ⓐ나는 아마 집에 도착하면 그가 나를 기다리고 있는 것을 발견할 것이다. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I think it is dreadful that anyone should be so miserable. I have piles of old clothes at home. Do you think he would care for any of them? His rags were falling to bits.”

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 그림을 완성했다고 답한 주어진 글에 이어, 같은 발화에서 늙은 모델이 Hughie를 궁금해해 그에 대해 다 말해야 했다고 덧붙이는 (C), 그 모델을 동정하며 헌 옷을 주고 싶어 하는 Hughie의 반응인 (D), (D)의 his rags를 them으로 받아 그 차림이 멋지다고 답하며 Laura 이야기까지 했다고 밝히는 (B), 사생활 누설에 분노하는 Hughie에게 그 거지가 유럽에서 가장 부유한 사람 중 한 명임을 알려 주는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

choices:
Q: How did the old model respond to hearing about Laura?
A: The old model showed little interest in learning about Laura.

Q: What did Trevor say when Hughie asked about the picture?
A: Trevor had not yet completed his painting of the old model.

A: Trevor told the old model nothing about Hughie except where he lived.

solution:
Trevor는 노인이 누더기를 입은 모습이 훌륭해 보인다고 하며 무슨 일이 있어도 그를 고급 코트를 입혀 그리지는 않겠다고 했으므로, ⑤ '화가는 그림을 위해 모델이 무엇을 입기를 원했는가? → Trevor는 모델이 이미 입고 있던 낡아 해어진 옷을 선호했다'가 알맞은 질문과 답이다.

④ Hughie는 그 늙은 모델을 위해 무엇을 하고 싶다고 말했는가? → Hughie는 그 가난한 늙은 모델에게 새 옷을 주고 싶다고 말했다. (→집에 쌓여 있는 헌 옷 중 일부를 주고 싶다고 말했다.)

And I must say he looked magnificent in his rags. Or perhaps I should say in my rags; they are an old suit I got in Spain.”

“A gold coin!” shouted Trevor and burst out laughing.
“You should have told me, Alan,” said Hughie. “Now I’ve made a fool of myself.”
“Well, when you came in, I didn’t know whether Hausberg would like his name (B)[mentioned / praised]. After all, he wasn’t fully dressed.”
“What a fool ⓔhe must think I am!” said Hughie.
“Not at all. He was in the highest spirits after ⓕyou left. He kept smiling to himself and rubbing his old, wrinkled hands together. (D)나는 그가 왜 그렇게 당신에 대한 모든 것을 알고 싶어 했는지 이해할 수 없었다, but I see it all now.”
Hughie (C)[sighed / cheered]. “The best thing I can do is go to bed,” ⓖhe said. “And my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone.” Hughie walked home feeling very unhappy.

body:
“Baron Hausberg!” cried Hughie. “Good heavens! I gave him a gold coin!” Hughie sank into the chair in shock.
“A gold coin!” shouted Trevor and burst out laughing.
“You should have told me, Alan,” said Hughie. “Now I’ve made a fool of myself.”
“Well, when you came in, I didn’t know whether Hausberg would like his name mentioned. After all, he wasn’t fully ⓐdressed.”
“What a fool he must think I am!” said Hughie.
“Not at all. He was in the highest spirits after you left. He kept smiling to himself and ⓑrubbing his old, wrinkled hands together. I couldn’t understand why he was so interested ⓒto know all about you, but I see it all now.”
Hughie sighed. “The best thing I can do is ⓓgo to bed,” he said. “And my dear Alan, you mustn’t tell anyone.” Hughie walked home feeling very unhappy.
The next morning, as Hughie was at breakfast, a servant brought him a card on which ⓔwere written “Monsieur* Gustave Naudin, messenger from Baron Hausberg.”
“I suppose he has come for an apology,” said Hughie to himself, and he told the servant ⓕlet the visitor in.
An old gentleman with gold spectacles and grey hair came into the room and said, “Do I have the honor of ⓖaddressing Monsieur Erskine?”
Hughie bowed.
“I have come from Baron Hausberg,” continued the messenger. “The Baron — ”
“I beg, sir, that you will offer him my deepest apologies,” stammered Hughie.
“The Baron,” said the old gentleman, with a smile, “has commissioned me to bring you this letter,” and he handed a ⓗsealing envelope to Hughie.
On the outside was written, “A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar.” Inside ⓘwas a check for ten thousand pounds.
When Hughie and Laura got married, Alan Trevor was the best man and the Baron made a speech at the wedding breakfast.
“Millionaire models,” remarked Alan, “are quite rare. But (A)model millionaires are even rarer.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓘ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓔ were written → was written (‘전치사+관계대명사’인 on which 뒤에서 주어와 동사가 도치된 구조이며, 뒤에 이어지는 주어가 카드에 적힌 문구 하나이므로 단수동사 was로 고친다.)
ⓕ let → to let (‘tell+목적어+to부정사’(~에게 …하라고 말하다) 구조이므로, 목적어 the servant 뒤에 목적격보어로 to let을 쓴다.)
ⓗ sealing → sealed (수식 대상인 envelope가 ‘봉해진’ 대상이므로, 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 sealing을 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 sealed로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 주어 he가 옷을 ‘입은 상태’를 나타내므로 dressed는 적절하다.
ⓑ keep의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사 smiling과 등위접속사 and로 병렬을 이루므로 rubbing은 적절하다.
ⓒ는 형용사 interested 뒤에서 '~하고 싶어 하는'의 의미를 완성하는 to부정사이므로 to know가 쓰인 것은 어법상 적절하다.
ⓓ 주어 The best thing I can do에 동사 do가 포함되어 있어 주격보어 자리의 to부정사에서 to를 생략할 수 있으므로 원형부정사 go가 쓰인 것은 어법상 적절하다.
ⓖ 전치사 of의 목적어 자리이므로 동명사 addressing이 쓰인 것은 어법상 적절하다.
ⓘ 장소를 나타내는 Inside가 앞에 놓이면서 주어와 동사가 도치되었으며, 주어 a check가 단수이므로 was는 적절하다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)model millionaires are even rarer가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Rich people who pose for painters are very hard to find.
Models who earn millions of pounds are extremely rare.
Wealthy people seldom attend the weddings of poor men.
Rich people who use their wealth kindly are harder to find.
Wealthy people rarely give any money to beggars.
solution:
남작이 '늙은 거지가 보내는 결혼 선물'이라며 Hughie에게 만 파운드짜리 수표를 보내고 결혼 피로연에서 축사까지 한 내용의 글이다. 앞의 Millionaire models는 거지 모델 노릇을 한 남작처럼 '모델이 된 백만장자'를, 어순을 뒤집은 model millionaires는 '모범이 되는 백만장자'를 뜻하므로, 남을 위해 기꺼이 큰돈을 베푸는 부자는 모델이 된 부자보다 훨씬 더 드물다는 의미이다. 따라서 ④ '자신의 재산을 남에게 선의를 베푸는 데 쓰는 부자들은 찾기가 더 어렵다.'가 적절하다.
오답
① 화가를 위해 자세를 취하는 부자들은 찾기가 매우 어렵다.
② 수백만 파운드를 버는 모델들은 극히 드물다.
③ 부유한 사람들은 가난한 남자들의 결혼식에 좀처럼 참석하지 않는다.
⑤ 부유한 사람들은 거지들에게 좀처럼 돈을 주지 않는다.

choices: a messenger's demand for an apology from a poor man
the importance of formal manners in greeting a visitor
a rich man's generous reward for a small act of kindness
Hughie's regret over wasting his money on a beggar

solution:

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Hughie was shocked to learn that he had given Baron Hausberg a gold coin.
Hughie felt foolish and believed that the Baron must think he was a fool.
Trevor burst out laughing when Hughie told him about giving the Baron a gold coin.
Trevor knew that Hausberg wanted his real identity to be revealed when Hughie came in.
Hughie thought Trevor should have told him that the old man was actually Baron Hausberg.
solution:
Trevor는 Hughie가 들어왔을 때 Hausberg가 자기 이름이 언급되는 것을 좋아할지 알지 못했다고 말했으므로, ④ 'Trevor는 Hughie가 들어왔을 때 Hausberg가 자신의 진짜 정체가 밝혀지기를 원한다는 것을 알고 있었다.'는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. (→Hausberg가 자기 이름이 언급되는 것을 좋아할지 알지 못했다고 말했다.)
오답
① Hughie는 자신이 Baron Hausberg에게 금화를 주었다는 것을 알고 충격을 받았다.
② Hughie는 자신이 바보 같다고 느꼈고, 남작이 틀림없이 자신을 바보로 여길 것이라고 생각했다.
③ Trevor는 Hughie가 남작에게 금화를 준 일을 이야기했을 때 웃음을 터뜨렸다.
⑤ Hughie는 Trevor가 그 노인이 실은 Baron Hausberg라고 말해 주었어야 했다고 생각했다.

body:
One morning, Hughie dropped in to see a great friend of his, Alan Trevor. Trevor was a painter. He was a strange, rough fellow with a bushy red beard. However, when he took up the brush, he was a real master, and ⓐhis pictures were eagerly sought after.
When Hughie came into the studio, ⓑhe found Trevor putting the finishing touches on a wonderful life-size picture of a beggar. ⓒThe beggar was standing on a raised platform in a corner of the studio. He was a wrinkly old man with a pitiful expression. He wore a ragged brown cape, and he leaned on a rough stick with one hand ⓓwhile holding out his hat for donations with the other.
“What an amazing model!” said Hughie, as he shook hands with his friend. “ⓔHow miserable he looks! How much does the model get for posing?”
“A penny an hour.”
“And how much do you get for your painting, Alan?”
“Oh, I get two thousand pounds for this!”
“Well, I think the model should have a share,” cried Hughie, laughing. “He is working just as hard as you!”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: people eagerly sought after his pictures
ⓑ: he found that Trevor was putting the finishing touches on a wonderful life-size picture of a beggar
ⓒ: On a raised platform in a corner of the studio was standing the beggar.
ⓓ: while he was holding out his hat for donations with the other
ⓔ: What a miserable look he had!
solution:
현재의 모습을 나타내는 현재시제 looks를 사용했지만, 전환한 문장은 과거시제 had를 사용하여 과거의 모습을 나타내므로 원문과 같은 뜻이 되지 않는다. What a miserable look he had! 자체는 문법적으로 가능한 감탄문이다.
오답
ⓐ 구동사 seek after가 쓰인 수동태 문장 his pictures were eagerly sought after를 행위자인 일반 사람들(people)을 주어로 한 능동태로 바꾼 것이므로 전환이 적절하다.
ⓑ 'find+목적어+목적격보어' 구문에서 목적격보어로 쓰인 현재분사 putting을 that절로 바꾼 것으로, 주절의 동사 found가 과거시제이고 Hughie가 작업실에 들어갔을 때 Trevor가 그림을 마무리하고 있던 중이므로 과거진행형 was putting을 쓴 것은 적절하다.
ⓒ 장소를 나타내는 부사구 On a raised platform in a corner of the studio를 문장 앞에 두면서 동사 was standing을 주어인 명사구 the beggar 앞에 둔 도치 문장이므로 전환이 적절하다.

body:
M: Hello, I’m Professor Noah Williams, and it’s a great honor to be here as a key speaker. With environmental pollution getting worse, sustainable cities are being suggested as a solution to the problem. Today, we will take a look at Copenhagen, one of the greenest cities in the world. Copenhagen, the capital of Denmark, has achieved a remarkable harmony between urban development and environmental conservation. About 62% of its citizens ride bikes to get around the city. Copenhagen has 546 kilometers of bike paths and bridges that allow people to go anywhere in the city by bike. Plus, renewable energy is being generated in a unique power plant called CopenHill. Each year, it converts 440,000 tons of waste into energy that can provide electricity and heating for 150,000 homes. Furthermore, Copenhagen’s buildings are covered with green roofs, where grass and trees are planted. These green roofs improve the air quality of the city and reduce its temperature. Let’s take a closer look at this remarkable city!
다음 담화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Professor Noah Williams introduces Copenhagen as an example of a sustainable city.
Approximately 62% of Copenhagen’s citizens travel by bicycle, using 546 kilometers of bike paths and bridges.
CopenHill, known as a distinctive power plant, generates renewable energy.
Every year, CopenHill transforms 440,000 tons of waste into energy for electricity and heating.
Copenhagen’s buildings with green roofs have little effect on the city’s air quality or temperature.
solution: 코펜하겐의 건물들은 잔디와 나무가 심어져 있는 녹색 옥상으로 덮여 있으며 이러한 녹색 옥상들은 도시의 공기 질을 개선하고 도시의 온도를 낮춘다고 설명하고 있으므로, ❺ ‘녹색 옥상이 있는 코펜하겐의 건물들은 도시의 공기 질이나 온도에 거의 영향을 미치지 않는다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

body:
G: Dad, we don’t have any shampoo at home. Let’s buy this brand. I saw it advertised on TV.
M: I think it’s ⓐbetter for the environment to buy one with this logo on it!
G: What do you mean by that? What does this logo have to do with the environment?
M: It indicates that the product is guaranteed not to ⓑcontain microplastics.
G: Oh, I read an article about the negative impact of microplastics on the environment. They are especially ⓒbeneficial to marine habitats because they eventually end up in places like rivers, lakes, and oceans.
M: That’s why we should consider purchasing products with this logo. It can ⓓencourage more companies to think about how they develop their products.
G: I never thought about it that way. From now on, I will be ⓔmore conscious about what I buy.
M: Great! Why don’t you check out other products with this logo?
다음 대화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓒ beneficial(유익한) → harmful(해로운, 유해한)

body:
When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some ⓐhelpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is (A)[why / what] Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer ⓑexperts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.
The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success (B)[that / which] the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to ⓒgrow in popularity, with more and more people (C)[signed up / signing up] to volunteer.
By ⓓproviding spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge ⓔnegative impact on our future.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ negative(부정적인) → positive(긍정적인)

(A) (B) (C)
choices: why / which / signing up
what / which / signed up

what / which / signing up
solution:
(A) be동사인 is의 보어 자리에서 완전한 절(Repair Cafés were started)을 이끌고 있으므로, 선행사 the reason이 앞에 생략된 이유의 관계부사 why가 알맞다.
(B) 명사구 such a success 뒤에 이어져 있으며, 결과를 나타내는 완전한 절(the idea soon spread to neighboring countries)을 이끌고 있으므로, ‘such a(n)+명사+that+완전한 절(대단한 ~여서 …하다)’ 구문을 이루는 접속사 that이 알맞다.
(C) ‘~가 …한 상태로, ~가 …한 채로’라는 뜻의 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)’ 구문을 이루어야 하며, 앞의 명사구 more and more people이 ‘신청하는’ 주체이고, ‘신청하다’라는 뜻의 sign up은 자동사와 부사로 이루어진 구동사이므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사를 사용한 signing up이 알맞다. 참고로, 자동사는 수동태나 수동을 나타내는 과거분사로 쓸 수 없다.

body:
On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, ⓐseriously damaging it. Although it still turns on, the screen ⓑis cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it ⓒrepair, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and ⓓpurchase a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing ⓔto do. If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ repair → repaired (have의 목적어인 대명사 it이 가리키는 her laptop이 ’수리되는‘ 대상이며, ‘have+목적어+목적격보어’의 5형식 구문에서 사역동사 have의 목적어와 목적격보어가 수동의 관계일 경우 목적격보어로 과거분사를 사용하므로, repair를 과거분사 repaired로 고친다. 참고로, 사역동사 have의 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동이면 목적격보어로 동사원형을 쓰고, 목적어의 행위에 진행이나 지속의 의미가 더해질 경우 현재분사를 쓴다.)
ⓓ purchase → purchasing (문장의 동사 자리에 might seem이 있으므로, 동명사구 getting rid of the old one과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 주어 역할을 하는 동명사구를 이루도록 purchase를 동명사 purchasing으로 고친다.)

body:
One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices ⓐare that they are too difficult to repair. For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it ⓑbe brought to an official service center to be fixed. Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. (A)소비자들이 그들의 물건을 고치는 방법에 대한 설명이나 수리를 완료하기 위해 필요한 부품들을 얻지 못하는 것은 흔하다.
The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that ⓒstates the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it ⓓyourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools ⓔrequiring to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers ⓕdesigning devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. Advocates of the movement say ⓖthat if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated. Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries ⓗjoin the cause.
윗글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The right-to-repair movement seeks to reduce e-waste by empowering consumers to repair their devices.
Consumers’ limited access to repair information and replacement parts has intensified concerns over electronic waste.
Manufacturers are increasingly redesigning electronic devices to make repairs more accessible to consumers.
The growing difficulty of repairing electronic devices has prompted governments to impose stricter regulations on manufacturers.
The expansion of the right-to-repair movement reflects growing public pressure for greater corporate responsibility in product design.
solution: 많은 사람들이 고장 난 장치를 수리가 어렵다는 이유로 버리는 문제를 해결하기 위해 수리할 권리 운동은 소비자들이 직접 또는 원하는 기술자를 통해 제품을 수리할 권리를 보장함으로써 궁극적으로 전자 쓰레기를 줄이고자 한다는 내용이므로, 글의 요지로 ❶ ‘수리할 권리 운동은 소비자들이 자신들의 장치를 수리할 힘을 갖게 함으로써 전자 쓰레기를 줄이려고 한다.’가 알맞다.

body:
In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer ⓐinclude a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. (A)색상으로 표시되는 시스템뿐만 아니라 0에서 10 사이의 점수도 사용하여, 그 지수는 소비자들이 제품을 구입하기 전에 그것이 얼마나 쉽게 수리될 수 있는지 알 수 있게 해 준다. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that ⓑrepairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair.
The index ⓒdesigned to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when ⓓpurchased new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products ⓔmore easily to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely ⓕto spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world ⓖfollows France’s innovative lead.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 알맞은 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓐ 요구를 나타내는 동사 requires의 목적어인 that절이 당위(~해야 한다)를 나타내야 하며, 제안(suggest, recommend), 충고(advise), 주장(insist), 요구(require, demand) 등을 나타내는 동사의 목적어 자리에 온 that절이 당위를 나타낼 때 that절의 동사는 ‘should+동사원형’이나 should를 생략한 동사원형을 사용하므로, 주어 every manufacturer 뒤에 조동사 should가 생략된 동사원형 include는 알맞다.
ⓑ 명사절 접속사 that이 이끄는 절의 동사 자리에 will be가 있으므로, 이에 대한 주어 자리에서 동명사구를 이루는 repairing은 알맞다.
ⓕ ’~일 것 같다’라는 뜻으로 ’be+likely+to부정사‘를 쓸 수 있으므로, is likely 뒤에 이어진 to부정사 to spread는 알맞다.

body:
On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously damaging it. Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do. If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste.
What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. (A) Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. (B) To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. (C) In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. (D) Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. (E) Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.
*metric ton 메트릭톤(1,000kg을 1톤으로 하는 중량 단위)
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘이러한 이유로 이 문제를 다루기 위해 노력이 이루어지고 있는데, 이 중 대부분은 제품들을 수리하기 더 쉽게 만드는 것에 중점을 두고 있다.’라는 뜻으로, this reason(이러한 이유)이 가리키는 내용에 해당하는 것으로서, 매년 생산되는 전자 쓰레기의 양이 걱정스러운 속도로 증가하고 있다는 문제를 2014년과 2021년의 데이터 및 2030년 예측되는 수치를 통해 구체적으로 설명하는 내용 뒤이자, 주어진 문장에 언급된 문제를 다루기 위한 노력과 관련해, 전 세계의 현실성 있는 접근법을 살펴보자고 언급하는 문장 앞인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop? Imagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one. She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself. (A)______, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it. Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, as she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score.
(B)______, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: Alternatively / For instance
As a result / Nevertheless
Therefore / In fact
Conversely / Instead
Alternatively / In fact
solution:
(A) Liz가 필요한 부품을 온라인으로 주문해 직접 교체할 수 있었을 것이라는 내용 뒤에 가까운 수리 카페에 고장 난 장치를 가지고 가서 수리 방법에 대한 조언을 받을 수도 있다는 대안을 설명하고 있으므로 ‘그 대신에, 아니면’을 뜻하는 Alternatively가 알맞다.
(B) Liz의 사례를 들어 손상된 장치와 기기를 개인이 쉽게 고칠 수 있는 세상에 살고 있다면 여러 방식으로 쉽게 자신의 고장 난 기기를 수리할 수 있을 것이라고 가정한 뒤, 이러한 지속 가능한 세상은 우리가 함께 노력하면 누릴 수 있는 미래라고 말하며 앞의 가정적 상황이 실현 가능한 미래임을 강조하고 있으므로, ‘사실은’을 뜻하는 In fact가 알맞다.

By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés ______. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

encourage people to purchase newer electronic devices instead of repairing old ones
provide professional repair services that require people to pay for technical assistance

Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.
The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer.
By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future.

solution:
ⓐ 동사(dropped)가 있는 완전한 절(Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 앞 절의 내용이 ’손상시키는‘ 원인이자 주체이고, 뒤에 목적어로 대명사 it이 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 damaging이 알맞다.
ⓑ have의 목적어인 대명사 it이 가리키는 her laptop이 ’수리되는‘ 대상이며, ‘have+목적어+목적격보어’의 5형식 구문에서 사역동사 have의 목적어와 목적격보어가 수동의 관계일 경우 목적격보어로 과거분사를 사용하므로, 과거분사 repaired가 알맞다. 참고로, 사역동사 have의 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동이면 목적격보어로 동사원형을 쓰고, 목적어의 행위에 진행이나 지속의 의미가 더해질 경우 현재분사를 쓴다.
ⓒ If가 이끄는 조건 부사절의 동사 자리이며, 시간·조건의 부사절에서는 미래의 일을 현재시제로 나타내므로, 주어 Liz에 수일치한 현재시제 단수동사 throws가 알맞다.

body:
In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair.
The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to ______. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.

choices: alter the standards of the repairability index
label its products according to the repairability index
take into account consumers’ trust in the repairability index
consider various repairability indexes when pricing products
assess consumers’ purchasing patterns and loyalty to products
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.
The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer.

What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.
*metric ton 메트릭톤(1,000kg을 1톤으로 하는 중량 단위)

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: E-waste is a term for unwanted electronic devices and electrical equipment.
E-waste creates significant threats to human health and the environment because of its hazardous materials.
Global e-waste generation is escalating at a concerning pace, rising by more than 30% between 2014 and 2021.
Experts expect annual e-waste generation to decline steadily after 2021, reaching half its current level by 2030.
Many efforts to tackle the e-waste issue aim to improve product repairability.
solution: 2014년에 비해 2021년에 전 세계 전자 쓰레기 발생량이 37% 증가했으며, 2030년에는 매년 발생하는 전자 쓰레기의 양이 16년 만에 두 배가 될 것으로 예측된다고 언급하고 있으므로, ❹ ‘전문가들은 연간 전자 쓰레기 발생량이 2021년 이후 꾸준히 감소하여, 2030년에는 현재 수준의 절반에 이를 것으로 기대한다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair. For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed. Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs.
The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated. Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries joining the cause.

The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need. Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions. So they decided to put it to a vote.
When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, she encouraged them not to use the familiar voting method, but to try something different instead. After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method. The entire council was curious to find out if the different methods would yield different results.

Every council member was interested in observing whether employing varied voting methods would lead to contrasting results.

The Condorcet Method
Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves ⓐcomparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options. In this case, there were three pairs ⓑto consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C.
Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, ⓒvoted either ABC, ACB, or CAB. Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. As option A, the art show, ⓓwas preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner.
The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes (A)______. This is especially true in elections that ⓔcontains numerous options. It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over ⓕothers.

choices: 2개

solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓒ voted → voting (완전한 절(11 people preferred A to B)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 동사가 이어질 수 없으므로, 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 주절의 11 people이 ABC, ACB, CAB 중 하나에 ‘투표하는’ 주체이므로 능동을 의미하는 현재분사 voting으로 고친다.)
ⓔ contains → contain (주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끄는 주격 관계대명사 that에 대한 동사 자리로, 주격 관계대명사는 선행사에 수와 태를 일치시키므로 선행사인 복수명사 elections에 수가 일치되도록 복수동사 contain으로 고친다.)
ⓕ others → the others (선거에는 선택지가 정해져 있으므로 전체 선택지들 중에서 어떤 선택지를 제외한 ‘나머지 다른 선택지들(the other options)’를 의미하도록 범위가 정해지지 않은 불특정 다수를 가리키는 others 대신, 범위가 정해진 전체 집단 중 '남은 다른 대상들(전부)'을 가리키는 the others로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 동사 involve는 동명사를 목적어로 취하여 ‘~하는 것을 수반하다’라는 뜻을 나타내며, 뒤에 명사구 the voters’ preferences가 이어지므로 명사구를 목적어로 취할 수 있는 동명사 comparing은 적절하다.
ⓓ 글이 과거 시제로 쓰이고 있으며, 주어인 option A가 선호되는 대상이므로 과거형 단수 be동사가 쓰인 수동태 was preferred는 적절하다.

Its production costs were excessive, and it consumed a lot of fuel. Also, it was able to carry only a small number of passengers. In other words, it was never a (C)profitable airplane. Despite these problems, large sums of money continued to be invested in the Concorde. The governments and airline companies ⓑfunded it were (D)reluctant to admit that it was a failure. They were worried about wasting the money and other resources ⓒthat they had already spent on it. Eventually, after many years of huge losses, the Concorde made its last flight in 2003. The decision to keep operating the Concorde was the result of the “sunk cost fallacy.” Why do people fall for the sunk cost fallacy? Perhaps it’s the human instinct ⓓto avoid losses. However, sunk costs are costs that you’ll never (E)lose, regardless of what decisions you make in the future. If you realize your past decision was a mistake, accept the fact and move on. We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to ⓐwhat career to pursue. However, there are many situations ⓑwhich we must make decisions as a group. Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with ⓒdiffering opinions. Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and ⓓmore efficiently, and various voting methods ⓔhave been developed over time. The following story illustrates ⓕhow do these different voting methods work.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓑ which → where (완전한 절(we ~ group)을 이끌어 추상적 장소를 나타내는 명사구 many situations를 수식해야 하므로, 관계대명사 which를 관계부사 where로 고친다.)
ⓓ more efficiently → more efficient (make의 목적어 group decisions에 이어진 목적격 보어 자리로, 5형식 동사로 쓰인 make는 목적격 보어로 형용사를 취하여 ‘~을 ...하게 만들다’라는 뜻을 나타내므로 목적격 보어 자리에서 앞의 비교급 형용사 fairer와 등위 접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어 형용사구를 이루도록 비교급 부사 more efficiently를 비교급 형용사 more efficient로 고친다.)
ⓕ how do these different voting methods work → how these different voting methods work (동사 illustrates의 목적어 자리이므로 의문사 how가 이끄는 간접의문문이 와야 한다. 간접의문문은 ‘의문사+평서문’의 어순을 따르므로 how do these different voting methods work를 의문사 how, 주어 these different voting methods, 동사 work의 어순으로 쓰인 how these different voting methods work로 고친다.)

ⓐ 전치사 to의 목적어 자리이므로 ‘의문사(구)+to부정사’의 명사구를 이루는 what career to pursue는 알맞다.
ⓔ 주어 various voting methods가 ‘개발되는’ 대상이므로 부사구 over time(시간이 흐르면서)과 함께 과거부터 현재까지 어떤 상태나 동작이 지속되어 오고 있음을 나타내는 현재완료 수동태가 복수 주어에 수일치하여 쓰인 have been developed는 알맞다.

Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making.
It is obvious that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task. No voting system is flawless or clearly superior to another. (A) Whichever we choose will have pros and cons. (B) Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all. (C) Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, arguing that more complex methods deliver more accurate results. (D) All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make better decisions as a society. (E) When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ourselves.
다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: ‘결국, 모든 가능한 투표 방법을 이해하고 장단점을 따져 보는 것은 우리가 의사 결정 과정을 더 잘 이해할 수 있게 한다.’라는 뜻의 주어진 문장은, Ultimately(결국, 궁극적으로)를 사용하여 투표 방식을 이해하고 비교하는 행위의 핵심을 제시하고 있으므로, 이러한 모든 노력, 곧 모든 투표 방식은 의사 결정을 어렵고 비효율적으로 만들기 위한 것이 아니라, 우리가 집단으로서 더 나은 의사 결정을 내릴 수 있게 돕기 위해 고안된 것이라는 문장 뒤이자 주어진 문장에 언급된 ‘의사 결정을 더 잘 이해하는 것’을 다시 언급하며 의사 결정을 더 잘 이해할 때 우리는 더 나은 의사 결정자가 될 가능성이 더 높다는 내용으로 주어진 문장의 결과를 진술하기 전인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need. Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions. So they decided to put it to a vote.
When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, ⓐ그녀는 그들에게 익숙한 투표 방법을 사용하지 말고, 대신 다른 것을 시도해 보라고 권장했다. After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method. The entire council was curious to find out if the different methods would yield different results.
On the day of the vote, each possible event was given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert.”
Each of the 20 council members was given a voting slip and instructed to write down the options in order of preference. For example, if the charity concert was their first choice, followed by the bake sale and the art show, they would write CBA.
After every member had voted, the voting slips were counted. The results were as follows:

choices: Exploring Different Voting Systems to Make a Choice
How Advisory Teachers in the Student Council Help Students
The Best Way to Collect Student Preferences Without a Vote
The Purpose and Operation Process of the Student Council
Three Popular Fundraising Events for High School Students

As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were ⓒ[added to / subtracted from] the total. This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. The First-Past-The-Post Method
The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. Voters are given ⓐseveral options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes (A)[win / wins]. Neither the second nor third preference ⓑmatters at all, so they are ignored. This method is commonly used in political elections around the world.
The student council quickly ⓒdetermined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7.
The FPTP method is uncomplicated and ⓓtricky to understand, but it has a significant weakness. It is possible to win a vote without the support of the majority. That was the case here. According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to ⓔhold a charity concert. However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, (B)[which / what] equaled 40% of the total votes.
The Alternative Vote Method
Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting. For an option to win in the first round, it needs to get more than 50% of the first-preference votes. As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting (C)[required / was required].

body:
The Condorcet Method
Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves ______ In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C.
Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB. Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. As option A, the art show, was preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner.
The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes fails to select a winner. This is especially true in elections that contain numerous options. It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over the others.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: giving different scores to options based on their ranked position
choosing the most popular option without ranking any choices
comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options
repeating the vote until an option secures a majority of the total votes
holding a second vote strictly among the options who received equal votes

The Alternative Vote Method
Next, the council members examined the votes ⓐused the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting.
(A) As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total. This meant ⓑwhat option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. As a result, the bake sale would be the winner.
(B) ⓒAn option to win in the first round, it needs to get more than 50% of the first-preference votes. As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was required.
(C) Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, ⓓwith only 5 council members voting for it. Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes ⓔredistributed based on their second preferences.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것은?
solution:
ⓓ ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)’가 ‘~가 ...하면서’라는 뜻의 부대상황을 나타내며, 명사구 5 council members가 그것에 ‘투표하는’ 주체이자 vote가 전치사 for와 함께 자동사로 쓰였으므로 with와 목적어인 명사구 only 5 council members에 이어 능동 관계를 나타내는 분사 voting이 쓰인 with only 5 council members voting for it은 알맞다.
오답
ⓐ used → using (완전한 절(the council ~ votes)에 접속사 없이 이어져야 하므로 동사가 올 수 없고 분사구문을 이끄는 분사가 와야 한다. 의미상 주어 the council members가 사용하는 주체로 목적어 the AV method가 이어지므로 used를 능동 관계를 나타내는 현재분사 using으로 고친다.)
ⓑ what → that (타동사 meant의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(option B ~ only 9)을 이끌어야 하므로, what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
ⓒ An option → For an option (주절(it needs ~ votes) 앞에 접속사 없이 명사구(An option ~ round)가 홀로 올 수 없으므로, 뒤의 to부정사구(to win ~)가 문장 전체를 수식하는 부사구가 되어야 한다. 따라서 to부정사의 to win의 의미상 주어를 나타내도록 전치사 For를 붙여 For an option으로 고친다.)
ⓔ redistributed → were redistributed (등위접속사 and 뒤에서 절을 이루어야 하므로 주어 the 5 council members’ votes에 이어진 동사가 와야 한다. 주어가 ‘재분배되는’ 대상이며 뒤에 목적어가 이어지지 않으므로 redistributed를 복수 주어에 수일치한 과거형 수동태 were redistributed로 고친다.)

Imagine you are at a restaurant with a menu ⓐthat has hundreds of items on it. You feel (A)excited at first, but it quickly becomes overwhelming. You do not know what ⓑto choose. Your choice ⓒwould be much (B)easier if you could pick between beef steak and mushroom spaghetti. This simple example (C)illustrates “the paradox of choice.” Having too many choices actually ⓓmake it harder to make a decision. When we have (D)numerous options, we feel like we have to compare them all, and we can never be sure which would be the best choice. Plus, ⓔwhichever we choose may leave us (E)satisfied because we have missed out on so many other options. The paradox of choice can affect our decisions in all areas of our lives, from choosing the color of our socks to deciding on a major.

body:
We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to what career to pursue. However, there are many situations where we must make decisions as a group. Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with differing opinions. Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and more efficient, and various voting methods have been developed over time. The following story illustrates how these different voting methods work.
The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need. Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions. So they decided to put it to a vote.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: People face various decision-making situations, ranging from daily personal matters to career choices.
Making a decision as a group can be challenging because it requires addressing multiple conflicting viewpoints.
Voting serves as a useful mechanism to reach group decisions in a way that is both fair and efficient.
The student council had to choose among three potential fundraising events to support children in need.
The student council members easily reached a consensus on the fundraising method before holding a vote.
solution:

오답

When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, she encouraged them not to use the familiar voting method, but ⓐtried something different instead. After ⓑdoing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method. The entire council was curious to find out if the different methods ⓒwould yield different results.
On the day of the vote, each possible event was given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert.”
Each of the 20 council members was given a voting slip and ⓓinstructed to write down the options in order of preference. For example, if the charity concert was their first choice, ⓔfollowing by the bake sale and the art show, they would write CBA.
After ⓕevery member had voted, the voting slips were counted. The results were as follows:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓐ tried → to try (그녀는 익숙한 투표 방법을 사용하지 말고, 대신 다른 것을 시도해 보라고 권장했다는 맥락으로, tried는 등위접속사 but으로 문장의 동사인 encouraged와 병렬 연결된 것이 아니라, 상관접속사 ‘not A, but B’(A가 아니고 B)로 encouraged의 목적어 them에 이어지는 목적격 보어 자리의 not과 to use에 이어진 것이므로 tried를 to부정사 to try로 고친다.)
ⓔ following → followed (if가 이끄는 부사절 내에서 완전한 절(the charity concert ~ choice)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로 연결되는 분사구문을 이끄는 분사로, 의미상 주어인 주어 the charity concert가 빵 바자회와 미술 전시회에 의해 ‘뒤따르게 된’ 대상이므로 수동을 의미하는 과거분사 followed로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ 주절의 동사가 과거시제(was curious)이므로, 이에 시제를 일치하여 종속절(if절) 안에서 미래의 일을 나타내는 조동사 will의 과거형 would는 알맞다.
ⓓ 주어 Each of the 20 council members의 첫 번째 동사 was와 등위접속사 and로 연결된 동사가 와야 하며, 주어가 지시받은 대상이므로 ‘instruct+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)’의 수동 표현인 ‘주어+be instructed+to부정사(~하라고 지시를 받다)’를 이루어야 한다. 이때 반복되는 be동사 was는 생략할 수 있으므로 과거분사 instructed와 to부정사가 쓰인 instructed to write는 적절하다.

body:
The First-Past-The-Post Method
The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. Voters (A)[give / are given] several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins. Neither the second nor third preference (B)[matter / matters] at all, so they are ⓐ[ignored / considered]. This method is commonly used in political elections around the world.
The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7.
The FPTP method is ⓑ[complicated / uncomplicated] and easy to understand, but it has a significant weakness. It is ⓒ[possible / impossible] to win a vote without the support of the majority. That was the case here. According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert. However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, which (C)[equaling / equaled] 40% of the total votes.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: give / matters / equaled
are given / matters / equaled
are given / matters / equaling
give / matter / equaled
are given / matter / equaling
solution:
(A) 맥락상 주어인 Voters(투표자들)가 여러 선택지를 ‘받는’ 대상이므로, ‘give+A(간접목적어)+B(직접목적어)’(A에게 B를 주다)의 4형식에서 A가 주어 자리로 나가 수동태로 전환된 ‘A be given B’(A에게 B가 주어지다)가 되어야 한다. 따라서 수동태(be+p.p.)인 are given이 알맞다.
(B) 상관접속사 ‘neither A nor B’(A도 B도 아닌)가 주어 자리에 올 때 동사는 B에 수를 일치시키므로, 단수 주어 third preference에 일치한 단수동사 matters가 알맞다.
(C) which는 콤마 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끄는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로, 관계사절 안에 동사가 없으므로 which에 대한 동사가 와야 한다. 따라서 동사로 쓰일 수 있는 과거형 동사 equaled가 알맞다.

body:
The Alternative Vote Method
Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting. (A)어떤 선택지가 1차 집계에서 승리하기 위해서는, 1지망 표의 50% 이상을 얻어야 한다. As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was required.
Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it. Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences. As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total. This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. As a result, the bake sale would be the winner.
Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either. (B)It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes. In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (B)It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes.가 의미하는 바로 알맞은 것은?
choices: First-round results are discarded, and a completely new vote is held.
Voters are forced to change their primary choices during the second round of counting.
The winner in the first round counting receives all the votes eliminated in the first round.
Candidates with fewer first-preference votes can ultimately win by gathering secondary support.
Second-preference votes are given twice as much weight as first-preference votes in every round of counting.
solution:
선택지 B(7표)가 1지망 표에서는 선택지 C(8표)보다 적었지만, 1차 탈락자인 선택지 A의 2지망 표(4표)를 흡수하여 최종 11표로 승리했으므로, ‘그것은 때때로 2지망 표가 1지망 표보다 더 큰 영향력을 갖게 하기도 한다.’라는 것은 1지망 득표수가 적었던 선택지가 2지망 표의 영향력 덕분에 역전하여 승리할 수 있음을 의미한다. 따라서 ④ ‘1지망 표가 더 적은 후보가 결국 차선책의 지지를 모아 승리할 수 있다.’가 (B)가 의미하는 바로 알맞다.
오답
① 1차 투표 결과는 폐기되고, 완전히 새로운 투표가 진행된다.
② 투표자들은 2차 집계 과정에서 1지망 선택을 바꿔야만 한다.
③ 1차 집계의 승자는 1차에서 탈락한 모든 표를 받는다.
⑤ 2지망 선호 표는 투표 집계마다 1지망 선호 표보다 두 배의 가중치를 부여받는다.

The Condorcet Method
Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options. In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C.
Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB. Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. (B) ______
(C) ______
answer:

(B) option A, the art show[또는 option A 또는 the art show]

choices: voters are required to limit their choices to only two options

solution:
콩도르세 방식은 선택지 쌍에 대한 투표자들의 선호도를 비교하는 것을 포함하며, 그것의 약점 중 하나로 종종 승자를 가려내지 못하는 것을 언급했으므로, 1대1 비교에서 모두를 이기는 절대적 승자가 없는 일이 발생할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ③ ‘1대1 비교에서 어떤 단 하나의 선택지도 다른 모든 선택지를 이기지 못한다’가 빈칸에 알맞다.
